title: the release guard's heredoc and quote reading, from BUG-15 through BUG-16
desiredOutcome: guard-release.py's cwd placement and publish detection are heredoc-aware and quote-aware, both bugs closed

findings.issue: BUG-15 as filed: _shell_moves read raw command text, so a file-data heredoc body containing a cd-shaped line was read as a real directory change. BUG-16 as filed: _publishers tracked no quote state, so a publish-shaped phrase inside any quoted text or heredoc body was read as a real publish.
findings.resolution: fixed in 7f8a9fd2: _shell_moves fed runnable_text; _publishers rewritten to match only against command_clauses's own, heredoc-stripped, quote-safe clauses.

findings.issue: 7f8a9fd2 fixed the cwd-absent branch only; _session_base's cwd-present branch still called effective_cwd with raw command text, so the identical heredoc-blindness survived there - a real release command could be placed in a tree the heredoc only pretended to cd into.
findings.resolution: fixed in cc40dae8: _session_base's cwd-present branch also feeds effective_cwd runnable_text.

findings.issue: cc40dae8's fix relied on runnable_text, which keeps a shell/code heredoc body but REORDERS it to the end of the returned text - so a decoy heredoc cd, placed anywhere in the command, could outrank a real, earlier cd to a bug-holding tree. Confirmed end-to-end with real git worktrees: a decoy bash heredoc let a release past an open high bug.
findings.resolution: fixed in 783648bb: effective_cwd now strips every heredoc body itself (via split_heredocs) before its ordered cd-walk, rather than relying on runnable_text's reordered view.

findings.issue: 783648bb's blanket heredoc-discard was wrong for eval: `eval "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"` genuinely executes in the CURRENT shell (confirmed live with bash -c), but was discarded as if it only ever moved a child process - so the same class of bypass survived via eval instead of a decoy heredoc.
findings.resolution: fixed in 5898818e: effective_cwd now answers the whole command's directory UNKNOWN whenever any heredoc body is graded 'shell' (named shell binary or eval/indirection), rather than discarding it.

findings.issue: 5898818e's 'shell' bucket did not recognize source or . (dot-source) reading a heredoc/stdin directly - no $(...) involved, so _HEAD_INDIRECTION never fired either, and _SHELL_PROGRAMS/_STDIN_SHELL had never listed source/. - silently graded as data. Confirmed live: source /dev/stdin <<EOF really moves the calling shell; effective_cwd answered with the stale starting directory instead of UNKNOWN.
findings.resolution: fixed in 251232c7: source and . added to _SHELL_PROGRAMS and _STDIN_SHELL, the same recognition bash/sh/zsh already had.

findings.issue: 251232c7's own fix for the bare dot-source had no position anchor, so _STDIN_SHELL's new `.` alternative matched a trailing `.`/`..` ANYWHERE at the end of a heredoc head - ordinary commands (git add ., cp file.txt ., cd .., rsync -av src/ .) sharing a line with any unrelated heredoc were misclassified as shell, over-refusing everyday work.
findings.resolution: fixed in fc7210f6: only the bare `.` alternative is anchored to start-of-head or a real command separator; the named programs (bash/sh/zsh/source) and all of _STDIN_INTERP are explicitly left unanchored, because narrowing those breaks an existing, deliberately-pinned test (gh35: a redirect target merely ending in an interpreter's name, e.g. cat > probe.sh, must stay graded as code/shell, since guard-secrets-read.py shares this classification and must stay conservative in the opposite risk direction).

findings.issue: The fc7210f6 fix also surfaced (not fixed, deliberately) a sibling gap: _STDIN_INTERP has the identical unanchored-trailing-word shape for interpreter names (mv a.js b.node, touch report.php both still match on the file extension) - and a permanent, structurally unreachable residual: a bare variable reference built from an earlier substitution used later in command position (x=$(cat <<'EOF'...); $x) is a data-flow question no lexical reader here answers.
findings.resolution: not a fix - both are documented as accepted residuals (SECURITY.md) rather than chased: the first is gh35's class (over-matching is the safe, intentional direction for guard-secrets-read); the second is the same structurally-unbounded-in-principle residual this file's SECURITY.md already opens with. CONTRIBUTING.md adds the -F <path> convention for any history-rewrite or release commit message as the practical mitigation.

review.outcome: matches; four independent defensive review rounds on the final rounds, no blocking finding on the tip [findings: 7 - 5 high, 1 med, 1 low; 0 with a recorded fix commit]

summary: BUG-15 and BUG-16 fixed across seven rounds of fix-then-review; final review clean; merged into main via P99
